facts.claim: British Airways flight BA252, a Boeing 777-200ER registered G-VIID, departed Nassau on Tuesday for London Heathrow on Wednesday and encountered strong upper-level winds; while cruising at 38,000 feet it reached approximately 282 knots, around 7-10 knots above its applicable operational limit.

The crew climbed to 39,000 feet and then 41,000 feet to find more favourable conditions; the flight continued to its destination and landed at Heathrow at 11:13 GMT on Wednesday after seven hours and 57 minutes, with no injuries or structural damage reported in connection with BA252.

Several other transatlantic aircraft experienced similar overspeed alerts during the same period, but available open-source information did not provide individual flight numbers or details of the circumstances.

According to the UK Met Office, the jet stream is a narrow band of powerful winds approximately five to seven miles (26,400-36,960 feet) above the Earth's surface, generally travelling from west to east.

According to Aerospace Global News, jet streams can reach speeds exceeding 250 mph (402 km/h); in February 2024 two Boeing 787 Dreamliners operated by Virgin Atlantic and United Airlines recorded ground speeds exceeding 800 mph (1,287 km/h), about 802 mph and 838 mph respectively, without exceeding their aerodynamic operating speeds.

According to NASA, tailwinds increase ground speed rather than automatically increasing airspeed, while sudden changes in wind direction or velocity, known as wind shear, can temporarily affect indicated airspeed; the report does not establish the exact aerodynamic mechanism behind the British Airways overspeed.

Clear-air turbulence can occur without visible clouds or thunderstorms and is frequently linked to jet streams; according to Aerospace Global News, conventional onboard weather radar cannot directly detect it, so pilots must rely on forecasts, reports from other aircraft and air traffic control.

zh.title: 強勁噴射氣流引發跨大西洋航班超速示警，英航777一度超出速限
zh.summary: 上週北大西洋上空強勁噴射氣流導致多架跨大西洋航班出現超速示警，其中英航BA252波音777-200ER在3萬8千呎巡航時一度超出適用操作速限約7至10節；機組改飛較高高度後航班平安抵達倫敦希斯洛，無人受傷、航機無損。
body: 上週橫越大西洋的航班遭遇異常強勁的噴射氣流，多架飛機據報出現超速示警。其中英航BA252由波音777-200ER執飛，註冊編號G-VIID，週二自拿騷林登平林德國際機場起飛、週三飛往倫敦希斯洛（LHR）途中遭遇強烈高空風；飛機在3萬8千呎巡航時速度一度達到約282節，較適用操作速限高出約7至10節。
機組先後爬升至3萬9千呎與4萬1千呎，尋找較有利的大氣條件以穩定速度；航班未再傳出問題，於週三格林威治時間11時13分降落希斯洛，飛行時間7小時57分。同期另有多架跨大西洋航班出現類似超速示警，但公開資料未提供個別航班編號或細節；BA252事件未造成人員受傷或結構損傷。

噴射氣流是高空狹窄的強風帶，據英國氣象局說法，約在地表上空5至7英里（約26400至36960呎）處，大致由西向東流動；風速可超過每小時250英里（402公里），為東向航班帶來強勁順風、縮短航程，但風向風速驟變（風切）可能短暫影響指示空速。報導提醒，機尾順風提高的是地速而非必然提高空速，噴射氣流與此次英航超速示警之間的確切空氣動力機制，現有報導並未確立。與噴射氣流相關的晴空亂流可能在無雲無雷雨的情況下出現，機載氣象雷達無法直接偵測，飛行員須仰賴預報、他機報告與航管資訊預判。

en.title: Strong jet stream triggers overspeed alerts on transatlantic flights; BA 777 briefly exceeds limit
en.summary: Unusually strong jet stream conditions over the North Atlantic last week triggered overspeed alerts on several transatlantic flights, including British Airways flight BA252, a Boeing 777-200ER that briefly flew about 7-10 knots above its applicable operating limit. The crew climbed to a higher altitude and the flight landed safely at London Heathrow, with no injuries or damage reported.
body: Transatlantic flights encountered unusually strong jet stream conditions last week, with several aircraft reportedly experiencing overspeed alerts while crossing the Atlantic. Among them was British Airways flight BA252, operated by a Boeing 777-200ER registered G-VIID, which departed Lynden Pindling International Airport (NAS) in Nassau on Tuesday for London Heathrow (LHR) on Wednesday. While cruising at 38,000 feet, the aircraft reportedly reached approximately 282 knots, around 7-10 knots above its applicable operational limit.

The flight crew responded by changing altitude, initially climbing to 39,000 feet before subsequently reaching 41,000 feet, to find more favourable atmospheric conditions and stabilise the aircraft's speed. The flight continued to its destination without further reported complications, landing at Heathrow at 11:13 GMT on Wednesday after seven hours and 57 minutes. Several other transatlantic aircraft experienced similar overspeed alerts during the same period, although available open-source information did not provide individual flight numbers or details. No injuries or structural damage were reported in connection with BA252.

The jet stream is a narrow band of powerful winds approximately five to seven miles (26,400-36,960 feet) above the Earth's surface, generally travelling from west to east, according to the UK Met Office. Jet streams can reach speeds exceeding 250 mph (402 km/h), providing strong tailwinds for eastbound aircraft. In February 2024, two Boeing 787 Dreamliners operated by Virgin Atlantic and United Airlines recorded ground speeds exceeding 800 mph (1,287 km/h) while crossing the Atlantic, about 802 mph and 838 mph respectively, without exceeding their aerodynamic operating speeds. Tailwinds increase ground speed rather than automatically increasing airspeed, according to NASA, but sudden changes in wind direction or velocity, known as wind shear, can temporarily affect indicated airspeed, and the precise relationship between the jet stream and the reported British Airways overspeed requires caution: the available report does not establish the exact aerodynamic mechanism. Clear-air turbulence, often associated with jet stream activity, can occur without visible clouds or thunderstorms and cannot be directly detected by conventional onboard weather radar, so pilots must rely on forecasts, reports from other aircraft and air traffic control.
